source_map.selection: mmq.cu:267-374 selects MMQ on RDNA3; Q8_0 falls through the always-true RDNA3 default
source_map.activation_layout: mmq.cuh:22-58 and 61-97 select block_q8_1_mmq D4 for Q8_0: four FP32 scales followed by 128 int8 values
source_map.activation_quantizer: quantize.cu:277-372 quantizes four F32 values per thread, computes one FP32 scale per 32 values, and writes the transposed 144-byte D4 block
source_map.weight_staging: mmq.cuh:774-833 loads eight raw Q8_0 blocks (256 K values) for 128 output rows into a padded row-major shared tile
source_map.dot_body: mmq.cuh:1159-1214 loads 16x8 signed-int tiles and accumulates a 16x16 int tile; mma.cuh:1306-1335 emits two RDNA3 wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu8_w32 calls per 32-K scale interval
source_map.outer_tile: mmq.cuh:3446-3520 stages one 256-K weight tile and two 128-K activation tiles, then accumulates FP32 scaled dots
source_map.launch: mmq.cuh:3930-4138 chooses mmq_x=128 subject to shared-memory fit and launches block=(32,8,1), mmq_y=128 on RDNA3

decomposition.wave_mapping: For mmq_x=128, waves are paired. A pair owns 32 output rows; the two waves own alternating 16-token column slices. Each wave walks four 32-token groups and two 16-row output minitiles.
decomposition.accumulation: Integer WMMA products are multiplied by the FP32 D4 activation scale and FP16 Q8_0 weight scale for each 32-K interval, then accumulated in FP32.

shared_layout_bytes.note: Only one 128-K activation half is resident at a time; the outer loop loads and consumes two halves around synchronization boundaries.

layout_crosswalk.raw_q8_0: llama.cpp starts from output-major raw block_q8_0[output, k_block] and transposes/pads each 128x256 tile into shared memory.
layout_crosswalk.hipengine_q8t16: hipEngine stores the same bytes losslessly as tiles[out_tile16, k_block, 16 fp16 scales + 32x16 int8]. It can populate the same logical shared tile without a resident raw sidecar, but requires a cooperative T16-to-shared transpose.
layout_crosswalk.rejected_lcp3b_difference: LCP-3B used two waves and a 64-output x 32-token direct geometry with ordinary 36-byte Q8_1 blocks. It did not stage/reuse a 128x256 weight tile or a 128-token D4 activation tile and therefore did not test the source MMQ schedule.

candidate.scope: standalone dense Q8T16 BF16-output diagnostic; no runtime routing before all leaf gates
candidate.design: Reproduce the source 128-output x 128-token, 256-thread, K256 shared MMQ decomposition over resident Q8T16 bytes and a source-compatible D4 activation pack.
candidate.red: A separately callable/registered MMQ128 D4 variant must not exist before implementation.
performance_gates: On W7900 512x2048x8192, the prequantized body must beat production two-wave FP16 WMMA in a cache-cycled HIP-event A/B.
D4 quantization plus the body must also beat production on the primary leaf.

An advancing candidate must then win all measured pp512 dense-Q8 shape classes and show the expected 256-thread kernel, zero scratch, bounded shared memory, and plausible register count under rocprofv3.
Only then may model routing and unchanged semantic/decode plus 512/4K full-model floors be tested.

decision: Proceed with exactly one standalone source-faithful MMQ128 screen. Do not retry direct T16 integer WMMA, independent-wave widening, raw-sidecar dp4a, selected Q4/Q5 retuning, or generic launch-count work.
